name: Ambrai
why_it_matters: Lakeside terrace below the 300-year-old Amet Haveli — the only restaurant in Udaipur that puts the City Palace, Jagdish Temple, Lake Palace and Jag Mandir all in one camera frame. A Khirni tree at the centre is the dining room's roof.
insider_tip: There's a ₹2,000 cover for the lakeside row — book 7-10 days ahead for sunset (5:30-7pm) or you'll be on the back balcony. Boats from City Palace ghat run through dusk.
signature_address: Amet Haveli, Outside Chandpole, Hanuman Ghat, Udaipur 313001

name: Upré by 1559 AD
why_it_matters: Rooftop of Lake Pichola Hotel — a row of dozen-odd candlelit cabanas with direct sightlines to City Palace, Jag Mandir and the lit-up old city. Run by the same family as 1559 AD, named after the year Maharana Udai Singh II founded Udaipur.
insider_tip: Time arrival for 30 minutes before sunset; the Aravalli light on City Palace's white facade is the dish here. Reservations are tight from October to March.
signature_address: Lake Pichola Hotel, Outside Chandpole, Udaipur 313001

name: Jaiwana Haveli Rooftop Restaurant
why_it_matters: Fourth floor of Jaiwana Haveli on the eastern shore of Lake Pichola — split between an open-air terrace and a glass-walled indoor room so the lake view stays even when the wind picks up. A few minutes' walk from City Palace and Bagore-ki-Haveli.
insider_tip: The indoor wing is the better seat in May-June (heat) and July-August (rain) — same view, no flies. Skip the Italian section; lean Mewari.
signature_address: 14, Jaiwana House, Lal Ghat, Chandpole, Udaipur 313001

name: Cafe Edelweiss
why_it_matters: Tiny German bakery near Bagore-ki-Haveli — fresh-baked cheesecakes and proper sourdough by 8am, espresso pulled from a small Italian machine. Long-time Udaipur backpacker breakfast spot, ranked top-3 desserts in the city on TripAdvisor.
insider_tip: Open 8am-8pm; the cheesecake stock sells out by mid-afternoon during high season — go before noon for first pick. Two seating tables only — most regulars take it away to Gangaur Ghat steps.

name: Charcoal by Carlsson
why_it_matters: Pratap Bhawan rooftop on Lal Ghat — Udaipur's only dedicated barbecue/charcoal kitchen, plus a Mexican soft-taco wing. Direct view of Jag Mandir and Lake Pichola; one of the few rooftops with an elevator.
insider_tip: Use the elevator in Pratap Bhawan — the four-floor walk-up keeps the average diner age young. Charcoal items take 25 minutes; order starters before sitting down.
signature_address: 12, Lal Ghat Road, behind Jagdish Temple, Silawatwari, Udaipur 313001

name: Namaste Cafe
why_it_matters: Rooftop above Hotel Gangaur Palace, near Bagore-ki-Haveli. 80+ item menu balances Italian (proper arrabiata) and Mewari classics with Lake Pichola views — the daytime alternative to the heavy heritage-hotel dinners.
insider_tip: Climb to the top tier (not the second floor) — the second floor is enclosed and loses the lake. Lunch is the better slot; dinner is loud with returning Bagore-ki-Haveli show audiences.
signature_address: 339, Gangaur Ghat Marg, near Bagore-ki-Haveli, Hotel Gangaur Palace, Udaipur 313001
